predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 may accept a dense visual encoding when search and labels make the task completable, while agent 1 may reject the same surface because kind, selection, direction, or authority meaning collapses without color; agent 1 may prefer stronger redundant cues that agent 0 finds add cold-start noise.

Agent 0 may prefer search-first navigation that reaches SuggestedTrack quickly, while agent 2 may reject search as a substitute for a comprehensible graph structure; agent 2 may prefer focus-scene pivots that agent 0 finds obscure global orientation or increase steps.

Agent 1 may favor persistent legends, labels, and non-color cues across every scene, while agent 2 may find those cues visually overload a deliberately small focus projection; agent 2 may favor animated reorientation that agent 1 rejects under motion, focus, or semantic-implication constraints.
